title: Property-(P) devissage in a dg-module derived category
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(A,d)$ be an associative unital differential graded $\mathbf Z$-algebra: $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ is a graded ring, $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ is additive, $d^2=0$, and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right dg $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with degree-one differential satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at maps inducing isomorphisms on every $H^j(M)=\ker(d:M^j\to M^{j+1})/\operatorname{im}(d:M^{j-1}\to M^j)$. Its distinguished triangles are the mapping-cone triangles and its shift is $M[n]^j=M^{j+n}$ with differential $(-1)^n d_M$ and unchanged right action [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $\mathscr P$ be a property of objects of $D(A,d)$ invariant under isomorphisms. Suppose (i) $\mathscr P(\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i)$ holds for every small family with $\mathscr P(M_i)$ for every $i$ (including the empty family); (ii) for every distinguished triangle, if $\mathscr P$ holds for two of its vertices, it holds for the third; and (iii) $\mathscr P(A[n])$ holds for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. Then $\mathscr P(M)$ holds for every $M\in D(A,d)$. No countability assumption on $A$, the cohomology of $M$, or the coproducts is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0FQE, remark-P-resolution, conditions (1)-(3) and conclusion; its proof cites the property-(P) sequence and existence of property-(P) resolutions.

proof.text: Choose an arbitrary object $M$ of $D(A,d)$ and a representing dg module, also denoted $M$. By [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-resolution] choose a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to M$ with a filtration $0=F_0P\subset F_1P\subset\cdots$ exhausting $P$, graded-split inclusions, and dg quotients $Q_n=F_{n+1}P/F_nP\cong\bigoplus_{j\in J_n}A[k_{nj}]$. The resolution and every $J_n$ lie in the module universe, so hypothesis (i) applies to these families. The image of $q$ is an isomorphism by the defining localization of $D(A,d)$.

We prove $\mathscr P(F_nP)$ for every $n$ by induction. The empty family in (i) gives $\mathscr P(0)$, hence the case $n=0$. The direct sums of dg modules represent coproducts in $D(A,d)$ by [lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle]. Thus (iii), (i), and invariance under isomorphisms give $\mathscr P(Q_n)$. The short exact sequence $0\to F_nP\to F_{n+1}P\to Q_n\to0$ splits as graded modules by the chosen filtration. By [lem-sfb-dg-derived-admissible-triangles] it gives a distinguished triangle with these three vertices. From the inductive hypothesis and $\mathscr P(Q_n)$, condition (ii) gives $\mathscr P(F_{n+1}P)$.

source.place: Tag 0FQE, remark-P-resolution; Tag 09KK, section-P-resolutions; Tag 09K8, definition-distinguished-triangle.

proof.text: The degreewise colimit of the inclusions $F_nP\to F_{n+1}P$ is $P$: each homogeneous element lies in a filtration stage, and the maps agree on overlaps. Apply [lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle] to this sequence. It gives the distinguished triangle $S\xrightarrow{1-s}S\to P\to S[1]$, where $S=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}F_nP$ and $s\iota_n=\iota_{n+1}(F_nP\hookrightarrow F_{n+1}P)$. By the induction and (i), $\mathscr P(S)$ holds. The first two vertices therefore satisfy $\mathscr P$, so (ii) gives $\mathscr P(P)$.

source.place: Tag 0FQE, remark-P-resolution; Tag 09KL, lemma-property-P-sequence; Tag 0CRL, lemma-homotopy-colimit.

proof.text: Finally, $q:P\to M$ becomes an isomorphism in $D(A,d)$, so isomorphism invariance gives $\mathscr P(M)$. Since $M$ was arbitrary this proves the assertion. Only the filtration is indexed by $\mathbf N$; its successive free quotients and the original module need not be countable.
